# menu pointer-rest CONTROL reds on CI: boundingBox returns null

## Context

`test/playwright/component/menu/List.spec.mjs:272` — *"CONTROL: the same path closes the submenu when a rest counts on enter"* — reds intermittently in CI, on the trunk and on PR branches alike, with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'x')
    at travelDiagonally (test/playwright/component/menu/List.spec.mjs:219:37)
```

**Six occurrences in forty minutes**, across three authors' branches and the trunk twice — every failing `Engine Tests` run in that window names this arm:

| run | branch | when |
|---|---|---|
| [35083847694](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35083847694) | `dev` | 10:14Z |
| [35083275383](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35083275383) | `grace/18764-grid-native-cell-editing` | 10:08Z |
| [35082035821](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35082035821) | `grace/18764-grid-native-cell-editing` | 09:54Z |
| [35081079204](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35081079204) | `dev` | 09:44Z |
| [35080858673](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35080858673) | `grace/18764-grid-native-cell-editing` | 09:42Z |
| [35079749239](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35079749239) | `agent/18760-menu-keynav-cascade` | 09:35Z |

@neo-opus-grace reports it reddening her PRs four times independently (#18769 ×2, #18773), which is where the count above stopped being two.

The 09:35Z run's `components` job was re-run at the **same SHA** and passed (09:50Z), which establishes intermittency. The arm landed on `dev` with #18765 (`Resolves #18759`); #18766 does not touch the hover path, and `dev`'s own red rules it out as a cause.

Locally it does not reproduce — **117 passes, no red** (see AC-1 below for what was tried).

The standing cost is the usual one — a flaky arm on the trunk trains every author to re-run reds without reading them.

## The Problem

```js
async function travelDiagonally(page) {
    const
        share = await page.getByText('Share', {exact: true}).boundingBox(),
        print = await page.getByText('Print', {exact: true}).boundingBox();
```

`print` is `null` at line 205, and line 219 is where it is first read. A `null` here is **not** "no such element": `locator.boundingBox()` resolves the selector with `state: 'attached'` first, so a selector matching nothing times out rather than returning `null` (@neo-opus-vega measured exactly this while filing #18693, and the note is why this ticket does not start from "the submenu never opened"). `null` means the element **was** resolved and then had no box when it was measured — it left the document, or its subtree stopped generating one, inside the window between the two calls.

So the arm reads two rectangles across two round-trips, after asserting `toHaveCount(2)` in a third. Anything that removes or replaces the submenu in between nulls the second read. That is also a correctness problem independent of the flake: the two rectangles can come from **two different layout states**, so the "diagonal" the arm then walks is only as coherent as the interval between the reads — a submenu still settling yields a path neither rectangle describes.

What removes it is **not established**, and this ticket does not claim it. AC-1 is a measurement, not a reading.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/component/menu/List.spec.mjs:202` `travelDiagonally` — the helper, shared by the passing diagonal arm (`:256`) and this CONTROL (`:272`). The CONTROL differs only in `subMenuHoverDelay: 0`, which makes every `mouseenter` a rest immediately rather than after 200 ms.
- `src/menu/List.mjs#showSubMenu` reuses a cached submenu per record key and only re-mounts when `activeSubMenu !== subMenu`, so a same-item rest is a no-op; the removal, if it is one, comes from somewhere else.
- `src/main/DomAccess.mjs:272` — `align()` sets the subject to `hidden: true` when the target rect cannot be resolved; `:1336` — `syncAligns()` does the same when the target element has left the document, and `onDocumentMutation` (`:893`) calls `syncAligns` on any `childList` mutation that is not purely align subjects. A submenu aligned to an item node is therefore one stale node reference away from being hidden by the main thread. Candidate, not conclusion.
- A floating component sits at `left: -10000px` until aligned, which still yields a box — so "not yet aligned" does not explain a `null`.

## The Fix

1. **Reproduce with instrumentation before changing anything** — an in-page `MutationObserver` trail plus `mouseover` / `setConfigs` capture over the arm, run against CI-like conditions (the full `components` suite, not the file alone), the way #18721's overflow flake was taken from reproduction to mechanism. If the trail shows the submenu leaving, the defect is in `src/menu/` or `src/main/DomAccess.mjs` and gets its own leaf.
2. **Measure both rows in one page task** — replace the two `boundingBox()` round-trips with a single `page.evaluate` that reads both rectangles from one layout state and names which row it could not find. This removes the window by construction and makes a genuinely closed submenu fail as an assertion with a readable message instead of as a `null` dereference two lines later. The arms' product assertions (`toHaveCount(1)` here, `toHaveCount(2)` in the diagonal arm) stay exactly as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC-1** — **not reproduced locally, in 117 arm runs across three conditions**, all on macOS against `99ebfde7d8`:

  | condition | result |
  |---|---|
  | the `pointer rest` describe ×15 (the arm in its file) | 75/75 |
  | an instrumented copy of the arm's pre-travel reads ×40 at 6× CDP CPU throttling — in-page `MutationObserver` over `document.body`, capture listeners for `mouseover` / `mouseout` / `focusin` / `focusout` / `scroll`, and a wrapper over the main thread's `Neo.worker.App.setConfigs` to catch a `hidden: true` from `DomAccess` | 40/40, no trail printed |
  | the full `components` suite ×2, so the arm runs in its CI position (#241 of 291) rather than alone | 2/2 green on this arm |

  So the trail cannot be taken on this machine, and **this ticket's fix is therefore a fix to the measurement only** — stated here as the AC requires. The reproduction that remains is CI-side, and the fix carries it: the helper now reports the missing row and the live menu count, so the next CI red diagnoses itself instead of dying on a `null` property read. If that message ever names `Print` with a menu count of 2, the submenu was showing and the row was replaced; with a count of 1, the submenu closed — AC-5 then applies.
- [ ] **AC-2** — `travelDiagonally` reads both rectangles from a single page task, and a missing row fails with a message naming the row.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the changed helper is exercised red-first: with the submenu forced closed, the arm fails on the new assertion rather than on a `null` property read.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the full `components` suite runs clean locally, and the `pointer rest` describe survives ×15 with the change in place.
- [ ] **AC-5** — if AC-1 finds a product defect, it is filed as its own leaf and linked here; this ticket does not fix engine behaviour under a testing label.

## Out of Scope

- The hover and keyboard behaviour themselves (#18759, #18760) — the arms assert them correctly; only the measurement is at issue.
- PR #18766, which is green at `99ebfde7d8` and does not touch the hover path.
- Any other component-suite flake; this ticket names one arm.

## Avoided Traps

- **A blind `waitFor` before the read.** It would convert a transient close into a silent pass and leave the arm sampling an arbitrary instant — the same trap @neo-opus-vega refused in #18693.
- **Re-running until green.** The same-SHA rerun here classifies the failure; it does not discharge it.
- **Asserting the mechanism from source.** `DomAccess`'s hide-on-missing-target is the plausible candidate and the cached-submenu guard argues against a remount. AC-1 requires the trail.
- **Deleting the CONTROL.** It is what makes `subMenuHoverDelay` load-bearing in the diagonal arm rather than incidental.
